stanzas: ข้าวรพุทธเจ้า
เอามโนและศิระกราน
นบพระภูมิบาล บุญดิเรก
เอกบรมจักริน
พระสยามินทร์
พระยศยิ่งยง
เย็นศิระเพราะพระบริบาล
ผลพระคุณ ธ รักษา
ปวงประชาเป็นสุขศานต์
ขอบันดาล
ธ ประสงค์ใด จงสฤษดิ์ดัง
หวังวรหฤทัย
ดุจถวายชัย ชโย
orig.credit: Prince Narisara Nuwattiwong, revised by King Vajiravudh (1914); the Thai text as quoted in Wikipedia's article

stanzas: We, servants of Your Majesty,
bow down with heart and head
to pay homage to the protector of the land, of surpassing merit,
the one supreme Chakri,
great lord of Siam,
whose glory is exceeding and lasting.
Our heads are cool because of your royal care;
by the fruit of the grace with which you guard us
all the people are happy and at peace.
We pray that
whatever you desire be fulfilled as
your noble heart hopes,
as we offer you victory: chayo!
Kha wora phutthachao
ao mano lae sira kran
nop phra phumiban bun direk
ek borom chakkrin
phra sayamin
phra yot ying yong
yen sira phro phra boriban
phon phra khun tha raksa
puang pracha pen suk san
kho bandan
tha prasong dai chong sarit dang
wang wora haruethai
dut thawai chai chayo
rom.credit: Romanization: The Epoch Institute (Royal Thai General System of Transcription (RTGS))

scheme: Royal Thai General System of Transcription (RTGS)
notes: line 1: 'kha', servant, with 'wora phutthachao', literally 'excellent Buddha-lord', the royal form of address: the subjects speak of themselves as the king's servants.
line 4: 'chakkrin', the Chakri king (the dynasty's name, also 'wheel-bearer', a universal monarch).
line 7: 'cool head' is a Thai image of peace and safety.
line 8: 'tha' (ธ) is the royal pronoun 'he' or 'you'.
line 13: 'chayo', 'victory!', the cheer that ends the anthem.
